message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the 2003 Mr. Basketball America and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). LeBron is known for his versatility—he can score, rebound, and distribute the ball with equal proficiency—and for his longevity, maintaining elite performance into his late 30s.

Beyond the court, LeBron is a prominent philanthropist and entrepreneur. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which has donated millions to education initiatives, most notably the “I Promise” program in his hometown of Akron. He also launched the media company SpringHill Entertainment and has produced films and television shows, including the critically acclaimed series *The Book of Boba Fett* and the documentary *The Last Dance* (though the latter is about Michael Jordan). LeBron has been active in social justice causes, speaking out on issues such as police reform and voting rights.

In short, LeBron James is not only a basketball legend but also a cultural icon, business mogul, and advocate for community empowerment.
